text:
nina: observed a spike in 429s for tenant 'acme-inc' on dedicated capacity.

nina: rate-limited traces show requests landing in goldPool-default-1 (low qps) instead of goldPool-prod-3.

mike: when did this start? any recent deploys?

nina: ~1932104000 UTC; no prod runtime deploys in the window. Billing shows normal usage. Repro steps below.

nina: REPRO:
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -H 'X-Redwood-Tier: [gold,v1]' \
  -d '{\"input\":\"test\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# response: 429 {\"error\":\"quota_exceeded\"} header x-request-id: r-abc123
```

raj: interesting — the X-Redwood-Tier header has brackets. control-plane header parser maybe stripping commas/brackets -> policy matcher falling back to default.

sam: can we see control-plane logs for request-id r-abc123? infra-bot: log snippet attached: `route_eval: policy=match_tags; raw_header=\"[gold,v1]\"; parsed_tags=[]; selected_pool=goldPool-default-1`

mike: that parsing bug would cause tier mismatch and route to lowest capacity pool -> throttles. nice catch.

nina: mitigation: added a temporary router rule to treat empty tag list as \"fallback-no-throttle\" and routed acme-inc -> goldPool-prod-3. Applied at 1932104500.

raj: permanent fix: runtime-parsing change to accept bracketed CSV and strip whitespace. I'll make a PR and coordinate a canary. Assigning to @raj for patch, @mike for rollout plan.

mike: plan: patch + unit tests; canary on control-plane-canary region for 2 hours; monitor token-level latency and 429 rate. If green, roll to prod.

nina: QA: add prompt set to ensure tier header variations don't drop tags. Also check audit logs for any other tenants affected.

support-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1932104567; priority P2; linked to support ticket #5482.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: 1932104800 -> control-plane-canary, CI green.

sam: thanks. keep thread updated with postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
